rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable stimulant drug intoxication in abnormal thoughts or behaviour
rule_level_problems.problem: Every sign is an independent OR, so a single non-specific sign (nausea alone, sweating alone, pulse ≥ 100 alone, DBP ≥ 90 alone) in any patient with abnormal behaviour yields PROBABLE stimulant intoxication. Nausea and sweating are also withdrawal signs, so the same patient gets both probable diagnoses. The page box reads as a cluster; at least the non-specific items should need a companion sign (e.g. any2) or the issue should be recorded as a judgment call.

rule_level_problems.problem: 'Known alcohol/drug user' and reduced (not stopped) drug intake are not represented; only stopped/reduced alcohol and abstinence from drug misuse.
The stimulant list (tik, cocaine, mandrax, cannabis) is not used, e.g. known exposure to these substances does not support stimulant intoxication; out of scope as a note but worth recording.

summary: Every likely/consider conclusion on the page (urgent priority, stroke/TIA, delirium, mania, psychosis, stimulant and alcohol intoxication, withdrawal, poisoning, dementia) is encoded with existing SNOMED concepts and the right rule type. The most consequential issue is the stimulant rule's any-single-sign OR, under which nausea, sweating or pulse ≥ 100 alone gives probable stimulant intoxication. Smaller gaps: disorganised behaviour (psychosis), reckless (mania), asymmetry (stroke/TIA) and the known-user/reduced-drug wording (withdrawal) are not encoded.
